questions.prompt: After v.erase(std::remove_if(...), v.end()) is replaced by just std::remove_if(...) on a vector, what is true?
options: Only the first matching element is removed and the rest keep their positions
The size is unchanged; kept elements are moved to the front, tail unspecified
The matching elements are erased from the vector and its size shrinks
The call fails to compile because remove_if needs the container itself
questions.explanation: Algorithms see iterators, not the container; only erase changes the size.

questions.prompt: How many comparisons at most does std::lower_bound need on a sorted vector of 100,000 elements? Give an integer (ceil of log2(n+1)).
You must return the sample nearest in time to an arbitrary query t from a log of 10^6 samples built once. Which structure is the most suitable?
options: A vector sorted by time, searched with lower_bound
A std::set<int> holding only the sample ids
An unordered_map keyed by the exact timestamp value
A std::list scanned linearly from the first element
questions.explanation: Nearest-key queries need an ordering; a sorted contiguous vector gives O(log n) and the best locality. A hash map only supports exact keys.
questions.skillLabel: Choosing a container for nearest-key queries

questions.prompt: Samples (t=4, v=12) and (t=8, v=20) bracket the query t=5. What is the linearly interpolated value? Give a number with 2 decimals.
Which operation can invalidate every iterator, pointer and reference into a std::vector?
options: A push_back that triggers a reallocation
questions.explanation: Reallocation moves the elements to new storage, leaving the old addresses dangling.

questions.prompt: double kp = params["kp"]; where params is a std::map<std::string,double> that has no "kp" key. What happens?
options: An std::out_of_range exception is thrown by the lookup
A key "kp" with value 0.0 is inserted and 0.0 is returned
The behavior is undefined because the key does not exist
An empty optional is returned and kp is left uninitialized
questions.explanation: operator[] default-constructs a missing value; use find or at for read-only access.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would benchmark vector+lower_bound against std::map for 10^6 samples so that the result is trustworthy. Mention at least four controls.
rubric: Optimization on (-O2), same pre-generated random queries for both, warm-up pass.
Consumes the results (e.g. accumulates and prints) so the optimizer cannot delete the loop.
Repeats several times, reports the median, and states the machine; varies N to see the trend.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
